_comment: Wholly invented org. Nothing here is mined from a real store: a public repo should not carry anonymised private notes, and a scrubber is not a thing to trust with that. Facts share vocabulary on purpose -- an eval corpus where every fact is lexically distinct scores 1.0 forever and never detects anything.
text: PLACEHOLDER
Team Tideway owns the atlas-api service and its on-call rotation.
Team Harbor owns the beacon service and its on-call rotation.
Team Lantern owns the ledger service and its on-call rotation.
Team Tideway owns the gateway service and its on-call rotation.
Team Harbor owns the deployment pipeline tooling itself, but not the pipeline definitions individual services write.
A service must have an availability SLO defined before the promotion pipeline will let it reach production.
Synthetic checks for a service live in that service's own chart and are promoted with it, rather than being maintained centrally in the pipeline repository.
The promotion pipeline holds a release at the canary stage until the canary analysis reports green for ten consecutive minutes.
The promotion pipeline only picks up an image whose tag matches the release channel it is promoting into; a mismatched tag produces no freight and the deploy silently never lands.
A newly onboarded service can take one full reconciliation cycle to appear, because the app-of-apps picks it up before the child application syncs.
Deployment controllers run once per cluster rather than from a single central installation, so a cluster-wide outage cannot stall promotions everywhere.
Rolling back means promoting the previous known-good freight forward; the pipeline has no reverse operation and editing the live manifest is drift.
Production traces are head-sampled at ten percent, so a single request is usually absent and trace-based debugging needs an aggregate view.
Services emit structured JSON logs; a plain-text log line is dropped by the collector rather than being indexed as an unparsed blob.
An SLO burn-rate alert is only allowed to page if it carries a runbook link; alerts without one are routed to a review channel instead.
The atlas-api latency objective is stated at the 99th percentile, not the mean, because the mean hid a slow tail that customers felt.
The metrics collector drops any series missing the service and environment labels, which is the usual reason a new dashboard renders empty.
Objective documentation belongs next to the monitors it describes rather than in a separate wiki page that drifts.
Work merges to trunk behind a flag rather than living on a long-lived branch; a branch older than two days is treated as a review failure.
Commit subjects follow the conventional-commits form and carry a tracker reference, which the merge check enforces.
A change touching a directory with a CODEOWNERS entry needs review from that owning team before it can merge.
Generated manifests are regenerated rather than hand-edited; a hand edit is overwritten on the next generation run and the drift is silent.
Secret material is referenced by pointer from the secret store and never written into a manifest, even a private one.
Ledger write operations carry an idempotency key, because the retry path replays them and the original design double-counted.
Every outbound call from the gateway sets an explicit timeout; the library default is unbounded and caused a thread-pool exhaustion incident.
The atlas-api paginates with an opaque cursor rather than an offset, so a page boundary stays stable while rows are inserted.
Incident severity determines who is notified, not how hard the problem is to fix; a small bug with customer impact outranks a large internal one.
Postmortems name systems and decisions rather than people, and an action item without an owner and a date does not count as one.
An alert that can page outside working hours must be actionable by whoever is on call without escalation, or it should not page.
The command-line tools discover their configuration by walking upward from the working directory, so a scratch directory outside any project falls back to the user-level file.
Local development runs dependencies in containers rather than installed services, so a version skew between two engineers is a container tag difference.
Private cluster endpoints and the internal registry are only reachable over the VPN; an off-VPN failure usually surfaces as a name-resolution or certificate error rather than as a refused connection.
The beacon service runs on virtual machines managed by configuration management.
The beacon service runs as a container workload scheduled by the orchestrator.
Batch reconciliation runs in a nightly window and cannot be triggered on demand.
The platform serves from a single region and has no failover.
Alerts route through the legacy notifier before reaching the on-call schedule.
The shared build cache is keyed by lockfile hash, so a dependency bump invalidates it for everyone at once.
